Name: MLD's Keybind
Author: MLD210
Description:
[b][size=4]FEATURES[/size][/b]

[b]One table for everything[/b]
The vanilla side covers Action, Use Tool, Menu, Journal, Map, movement,
Chat, Emote, Run, Swap Toolbar and all twelve inventory slots, plus
Cancel. The modded side pulls in every key binding that installed mods
have registered with Generic Mod Config Menu - no per-mod patches, no
manually maintained compatibility list.
[img width=434]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54946/54946-1793610459-293253723.png[/img]
[b]Rebind in place[/b]
Click a key cell and press the key you want. Vanilla bindings are written
to the game's own options; mod bindings are handed back to the mod that
owns them, so each one saves through its normal config path.
[img width=458]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54946/54946-1793610506-792765407.png[/img]
[b]Modifier combinations[/b]
For mod options that accept a key combination, hold Ctrl, Shift or Alt and
press the final key to bind something like LeftCtrl + K. Existing
combinations are displayed as they are, so you can see the full bind
rather than just its last key.

[b]Nothing is written until you say so[/b]
Every change is staged first: pending rows are marked, the bar at the
bottom counts them, Undo removes the last one and Discard throws all of
them away. Only Apply actually writes to the game and to your mods.
[img width=595]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54946/54946-1793610570-1664034398.png[/img]
[b]Conflict detection[/b]
Any key bound to more than one action is highlighted, so a collision is
visible before you walk into it mid-fight. Conflicts are reported, not
blocked - the game itself allows duplicate bindings.
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54946/54946-1793610597-1266382497.png[/img]
[b]Search that keeps up[/b]
Type to filter by key, action name, mod name or mod ID. Start typing
anywhere in the table and the search box takes over; Esc drops focus and
keeps the filter.
[img width=473]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54946/54946-1793610621-1126395439.png[/img]

[b]Reset one binding, or all of them[/b]
Each row has its own Reset, and Reset All stages every binding back to its
default behind a confirmation dialog. For mod bindings the atlas works out
each mod's defaults from a throwaway copy of its config class, so resetting
one key does not wipe the rest of that mod's settings.

[b]Title screen and in-game[/b]
Some mods only allow their config to be edited from the title screen. The
table opens there too, and when a binding is locked in game the row is
greyed out with a tooltip that tells you where to go instead.

[b]Read-only rows explain themselves[/b]
Mouse buttons, secondary vanilla keys and fixed bindings cannot be
changed, but hovering them tells you exactly why, instead of silently
doing nothing.

[b]Localised[/b]
English and Simplified Chinese are included; the table follows the game's
language setting.


[b][size=4]REQUIREMENTS[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6 or later[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0 or later[/*]
[*]Generic Mod Config Menu - optional but recommended. Without it the
table still lists every vanilla binding, but mod bindings come from GMCM's
registry, so mods that do not use GMCM will not appear.[/*]
[/list]

[b][size=4]INSTALLATION[/size][/b]

[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Unzip this archive into your Stardew Valley/Mods folder, so that you end
up with Mods/MLD's Keybind/manifest.json.[/*]
[*]Optional: install Generic Mod Config Menu for mod keybind support.[/*]
[*]Start the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]
To uninstall, delete Mods/MLD's Keybind. Your key bindings stay as you left
them, because they live in the game's options and in each mod's own config.


[b][size=4]HOW TO USE[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]F9 opens and closes the table.[/*]
[*]Click a key cell, then press the new key. Esc cancels the capture.[/*]
[*]Hold Ctrl, Shift or Alt before the final key to bind a combination
(mod options that support combinations only).[/*]
[*]Press Apply to save the staged changes, Undo to drop the last one,
Discard to drop them all.[/*]
[*]Use the search box, or just start typing, to narrow the list.[/*]
[*]Click Reset on a row to restore that single binding; Reset All restores
everything after a confirmation.[/*]
[*]Esc closes the table - it first cancels a key capture, then the search
field, then the reset confirmation.[/*]
[/list]

[b][size=4]CONFIGURATION[/size][/b]

One setting, in Generic Mod Config Menu under "MLD's Keybind", or in
Mods/MLD's Keybind/config.json:

[list]
[*][b]Open key[/b] - the key that opens the table. Default: F9.[/*]
[/list]
The table itself needs no configuration: it is rebuilt from the game's
options and from GMCM's registry every time it opens.


[b][size=4]HOW MOD KEY BINDINGS ARE READ[/size][/b]

The atlas asks SMAPI for the Generic Mod Config Menu API, walks the config
menus GMCM has registered, and picks out the options whose values are keys
(a single button or a list of key combinations). Reading and writing those
options goes through the same objects GMCM uses, and each write triggers
the owning mod's own save callback - which is why changes survive a restart
and appear in that mod's config file.

Defaults are learned without touching your live settings: a temporary
instance of the mod's config class is created, its values are read, and the
real config object is put straight back. If a mod keeps its config somewhere
unusual and the defaults cannot be read safely, the atlas falls back to that
mod's own reset routine for the single key you asked about, then restores
every other option to the value it had before.


[b][size=4]COMPATIBILITY[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Client-side only. Safe to add to an existing save and to use in
multiplayer.[/*]
[*]No Harmony patches, no game code overwritten, no new assets.[/*]
[*]Works with any mod that registers key bindings through GMCM, including
mods whose config is title-screen only.[/*]
[*]Independent of UI mods - the table draws itself and does not depend on
Content Patcher, SpaceCore or similar frameworks.[/*]
[/list]

[b][size=4]KNOWN LIMITATIONS[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Mods that never register their key bindings with GMCM cannot be listed.
If a mod is missing from the table, that is almost always the reason.[/*]
[*]Mouse buttons and secondary vanilla keys are shown but cannot be
rebound here.[/*]
[*]Bindings can conflict; the table highlights them but will not stop you.[/*]
[*]A few mods store their config in a shape that cannot be inspected
safely. Their keys still appear, but they may be read-only or reset through
the mod's own routine rather than staged like the rest.[/*]
[/list]

[b][size=4]TROUBLESHOOTING[/size][/b]

[b]The table will not open.[/b]
Check that another menu is not already open, and that the open key is not
being swallowed by another mod. The key can be changed in GMCM.

[b]A mod's key bindings are missing.[/b]
Open the SMAPI console and look for lines starting with "Keybind:". They
say which config menus could not be read, and why.

[b]A mod's row is greyed out in game.[/b]
That mod only allows its config to be edited at the title screen. Open the
atlas from the title screen and the row becomes editable.

[b]A change did not stick.[/b]
Look for a warning in the SMAPI console naming the action and the mod - the
mod refused the write, and the log line says which one.


[b][size=4]CREDITS[/size][/b]

Made by MLD. Built on SMAPI and the Generic Mod Config Menu API by
spacechase0. Thanks to both for making mod configuration this accessible in
the first place.

Feedback, bug reports and missing-mod cases are welcome - the SMAPI log is
the most useful thing you can attach.
